'''''Helianthus praecox''''' is a North American species of [[Helianthus|sunflower]] known by the common name '''Texas sunflower'''. It is [[endemism|endemic]] to [[Texas]]. Most of the populations are either along the [[Gulf Coast of the United States|Gulf Coast]] or in the [[Río Grande Valley]].<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Helianthus%20praecox.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref>

''Helianthus praecox'' grows on sandy soils and coastal prairies. It is an annual herb up to 150 cm (60 inches or 5 feet) tall. One plant usually produces 1-3 [[Head (botany)|flower heads]], each containing 11-16 yellow [[ray florets]] surrounding 35 or more red or purple [[disc floret]]s.<ref name=crockett>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250066896 Flora of North America, Helianthus praecox Engelmann & A. Gray, 1847.  Texas sunflower ]</ref>

;Subspecies<ref name=austin/><ref name=crockett/><ref>[http://www.phytologia.org/uploads/2/3/4/2/23422706/962107-109turner_helianthus_texas_sunflower.pdf Billie L. Turner. 2014. Taxonomy of the Texas sunflower ''(Helianthus praecox)'' Asteraceae. Phytologia (April 1, 2014) 96(2) 107] includes county-level range map for all 3 subspecies</ref>
*''Helianthus praecox'' subsp. ''hirtus'' <small>(Heiser) Heiser</small> - near [[Carrizo Springs, Texas|Carrizo Springs]] in [[Dimmit County, Texas|Dimmit County]]
*''Helianthus praecox'' subsp. ''praecox'' - sandy soils along the coast in [[Galveston County, Texas|Galveston County]] + [[Brazoria County, Texas|Brazoria County]]
*''Helianthus praecox'' subsp. ''runyonii'' <small>(Heiser) Heiser</small> - Coastal prairies (from [[Calhoun County, Texas|Calhoun County]] to [[Cameron County, Texas|Cameron County]])  and [[Río Grande Valley]] (from [[Webb County]] to [[Cameron County, Texas|Cameron County]])
